messages:
Alex Kim: FYI — I'm proposing a synthetic traffic/probing run against the GPU inference fleet to validate our admission-control and queueing thresholds. target pool: gpu-pool-west1 (A100s). goal: validate behavior at 80/90/95% sustained utilization + short 110% spike to verify graceful degradation and fallback to cheaper variants.
Mina Patel: +1. Can you confirm what metrics we'll capture? GPU util, queue length, token-per-second, and per-request 429s?
Alex Kim: yes. core metrics: gpu_util, avg_kv_cache_size, queue_depth, admission_reject_rate (429), request_latency_p50/p95/p99, model_fallback_rate, and per-route error budget consumption. also collect kernel stall logs where possible.
Chris O'Neill: What tool are you using to generate synthetic traffic? we should avoid hammering the control plane.
Alex Kim: using a k6 job for steady ramps and a short locust spike for concurrency patterns. will run from a separate test cluster with NATed IPs to mimic customer traffic. command samples below:
```bash
# steady ramp (k6):
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 35m ramp-script.js --out json=steady-ramp.json
# spike (locust):
locust -f spike.py --headless -u 4000 -r 400 --run-time 5m --host https://api.redwood-inference.test
```
Sasha Ivanov: @Alex Kim please add a rate-limiter header so admission-control treats this like a normal tenant (X-Test-Tenant: loadtest). We need to ensure route-based policies apply.
Alex Kim: done — will tag with X-Test-Tenant and use the 'test-tenant' routing policy. also setting cost_center=test-load to keep billing separate.
infra-bot: notice — planned maintenance window conflict: auto-scaler-controller is scheduled for a config rollout in gpu-pool-west1 at 03:15 UTC.
Alex Kim: thanks infra-bot. we'll shift the run to 04:00 UTC to avoid overlap.
Mina Patel: two quick asks: 1) Can we pin one node group to prevent autoscaler from adding capacity during the ramp? We want to validate backpressure, not autoscale. 2) Cost estimate?
Chris O'Neill: For (1) use the nodegroup annotation `scale.k8s.io/disable-autoscale: 'true'` on the test nodegroup and set a taint so regular workloads don't land. For (2) rough calc: expected 3 GPUs * 4h at $3.50/hr = ~$42 plus data and control plane egress ~ $15. keep it below $100.
Alex Kim: plan: create a dedicated test nodegroup with autoscale disabled, cordon regular nodes from the test namespace. run ramp: 10m ramp->20m hold at 80%, step to 95% for 15m, then 5m 110% spike. total window ~1h.
Sasha Ivanov: what do we expect the admission policy to do at 95-110%? documented behavior: at >95% we should start soft-throttling new sessions (queueing), and above 100% we should hit hard rejection (429) and route to fallback variants (smaller model) for compatible requests. need to confirm the split ratio for fallback is 70/30 by default.
oncall-bot: reminder — run must be approved by oncall before starting. react with :white_check_mark: when ready.
Mina Patel: also capture per-shard enqueue_time and dequeue_time to compute effective queueing latency. will attach a tracing span with `x-trace-loadtest` so it shows up in Console.
Alex Kim: included. monitoring config:
```yaml
alerting:
  - name: queue-latency-high
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(queue_dequeue_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 1.5
    for: 10m
```
Chris O'Neill: One risk: network egress from test cluster might saturate the cross-region links if we use multiple regions. Keep test only in west1. Also make sure model cache warming is disabled so we don't falsely lower admission pressure.
Alex Kim: good call. we'll run single-region west1 and disable cache warm-up by setting `X-Cache-Warm: false`.
Sasha Ivanov: who will watch the run? I'll be on pager rotation and can monitor dashboards + take down the job if we see >2% production-impact signals.
Alex Kim: I'm the owner — will post the run link and k6 logs here. timeline: 04:00 UTC start (tomorrow), expected end 05:10 UTC. please ack.
Mina Patel: ack.
Chris O'Neill: ack.
Sasha Ivanov: ack.
Alex Kim: last note — if admission rejects exceed 20% for more than 10m we stop and record a regression ticket. Also will test the token-bucket config var: `admission.token_bucket_refill_qps` set to current prod value and then 0.8*prod to see difference.
Mina Patel: can you add the exact experiment matrix to the run doc? I'll review before greenlight.
Alex Kim: added: matrix includes three refill_qps settings (1.0x, 0.8x, 0.6x), two model variants (full, quantized-8bit), and two queue limits (1000, 2000).
Sasha Ivanov: sounds good. I'll leave a note on the run channel and monitor. thanks team. :rocket:
